observations: Photo 0 shows a single car headlight assembly wrapped in clear plastic film.
The design features a horizontal slat pattern in the center and a clear lens.
The plastic wrap is torn at the edges, suggesting it is not new.
No brand name, model number, or part number is visible on the unit.
The background is a dark, textured floor.

claims.claim: Original Toyota part, not China copy. No crack, all clips and brackets complete.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The headlight may be a generic aftermarket or non-OEM replacement.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's identification plate or the part number stamped on the housing.

risks.risk: The internal LED or HID bulbs may be missing or non-functional.
risks.proof: A photo of the internal bulb sockets and a video showing the headlight powered on.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring new bulbs and a controller

proof_requests: Close-up of the VIN plate, usually on the dashboard or door jamb.
Photo of the manufacturer's identification plate showing the part number.
Photo of the internal bulb sockets.
Video of the headlight turned on to confirm the LEDs work.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
